a) a sub-radix2 SAR ADC is proposed to reduce the effect of capacitor mismatch; b) a digital background calibration scheme is developed to compensate the non-idealities in the sampling switches, and the reference voltage settling problem; c) a DTC technique is developed to reduce the effect on linearity of the comparator offset.
a sub-radix 2 SAR ADC is capable of achieving a high dynamic range, and the proposed calibration technique and DTC technique can improve the ADC's performance.
a sub-radix 2 SAR ADC can achieve a very low power, high resolution, and good linearity, by using the proposed digital calibration and DTC technique.

this work presents a novel sub-radix- 2 SAR ADC architecture, which employs a digital background calibration scheme to overcome the non-ideal effects of the DAC, and a dynamic-threshhold-comparison technique to overcome the comparator offset issue.
this work presents a 12b 2.25MS/s 3mW 0m059mm2 CMOSP SAR ADC that achieves 91.3dB SFDR and 73.3dB SNDR at 1MHz input frequency with a 1.8V supply, while consuming 3mW.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a 12-bit SAR ADC with 22.5MS/s conversion speed is implemented in 0.11um CMOS process, which achieves over 90dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion-ratio (SNDR) and 93dB spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) at 5MHz input frequency, while occupying 0.059 mm2 chip area.

the DTC technique has been successfully demonstrated in a 90nm process, with a measured SNDR of 80dB, and an SFDR of 90dB at a 22.5MS/s sampling rate, while consuming 0.059 mm2 chip area and 3mW of power from a 1.2V supply.
the proposed SAR ADC achieves a 90dB SF DR, 12 b resolution, 22.5MS/s sampling rate, and a power consumption of 3.0 mW from a 1.2 V power supply.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a SAR ADC is not necessarily a linear ADC, and the linearity can be greatly improved by a simple digital post-processing scheme that is compatible with the existing SAR ADC.

the proposed DTC scheme is capable of improving the SFDR performance of a SAR ADC by more than 20dB at 22.5MHz sampling rate, while maintaining a very low power dissipation of 3mW and small chip area of 0.059 mm2.
a sub-radix2 SAR ADC can be implemented in a standard 65nm CMOS process with only moderate area and energy overhead.
